title: yaks core keyword vocabulary
description: The keywords the yaks meta-model adds to JSON Schema 2020-12 to describe a component vocabulary. Native JSON Schema still carries type, format, enum, const, default, description, examples, $ref/$defs; these keywords add what a component table needs on top. Native keywords reach the table too: `type: integer` stores with integer affinity, a component's `required` list is NOT NULL, `default` is the column default (`{"now": true}` for the clock), and `enum` is a CHECK. `examples` is native and subsumes the old `well` concept: a text field's completion draws from its examples union the column's own live distinct values.
$comment: A vocabulary declaration in the JSON Schema sense: a URI that names this keyword set, plus the schema of each keyword. A vocab file declares it under $vocabulary.

component.description: true = this $defs entry declares a COMPONENT: an object schema whose properties are the component's columns. Required — an entry that says neither this nor `tool` is an ordinary reusable subschema the loader never plants.

tool.description: true = this $defs entry declares a TOOL: one named thing an agent can ask the graph to do. Its implementation is the module's, keyed by the entry name (or noun_verb); the declaration is the part that travels.

noun.description: A tool's resource word, one lowercase word — what it acts on. A CLI answers to either order (`session list`, `list session`).

verb.description: A tool's operation word, one lowercase word — what it does. Always written together with `noun`.

input.description: A tool's arguments: one JSON Schema per named argument, the same shape a component's `properties` takes. The entry's `required` list names the ones a call must carry.

ref.description: The entity kind a string column references, e.g. "project" or "entity" (any entity). Makes the column a reference that stores the target's internal id.

death.description: What the reaper does to this reference when its target entity dies.

sync.description: Who hears about a write to this component. "server" (the default) sends it to the server, which owns it and fans it out to subscribers; "none" keeps it on the writing node; "peers" sends it to the server, which RELAYS it to subscribers without owning it.

durable.description: How long a value of this component lives, asked of whoever owns it. "forever" (the default) is storage — SQLite and the journal on a server, the vault in a client. "connection" is memory keyed by the writer's connection, swept when that connection closes. A duration ("5s", "2m") is that plus a timer, restarted on each write.

computed.description: true = this column is derived, never stored: no column holds it, nobody writes it, a reader still sees it (a query-only rank, an aggregate, a status read off marks). Default false — a column nobody declares is stored.

stamped.description: true = server-owned: readable but never wire-writable.

search.description: true = this text column is full-text indexed: its words are what a bare-word search matches, and a hit ranks by them. A column no one declares is stored and readable but never searched.

kind.description: true = this component names a display kind (feeds kindOf / kindOrder).

before.description: Kind names this kind sorts before. kindOrder is alphabetical, topologically refined by these constraints.

wire.description: false = a readable-not-writable component (the spine, `entity`). Default true.

bare.description: false = this column (or every column of this component) never claims its bare filter spelling; it is reached qualified only (.comp.prop). The declarative form of a lazy log partition, or of yielding a bare word an older concept already owns.

aliases.description: Input spellings that resolve to an enum member; output always speaks the canonical member.

unique.description: The uniqueness a race is decided by. On a COLUMN, true = no two rows of the component may share the value. On a COMPONENT, the composite uniques as column lists: [["space", "slug"]], or {"cols": ["key"], "present": ["key"]} for a unique over the rows that hold the key (a partial index).

identity.description: What the entity's own id is DERIVED from. On a COLUMN, true = this component's entities are identified by this value: the eid is sha256("<component>|<value>") worn as a UUID, so writing the same value twice is one entity and uniqueness is a fact about ids rather than a race. On a COMPONENT, the column list a composite identity is spelled across, in derivation order: ["space", "slug"]. One tuple, never a list of them — an entity has one id.

index.description: An index to read by, carrying no uniqueness. On a COLUMN, true = index it. Stored refs are always indexed: true is redundant and false does not opt out. On a COMPONENT, the composite indexes as column lists: [["app", "version"]], or {"cols": [...], "present": [...]} for a partial index over the rows that hold those columns.
